event: VAR introduced in the Premier League
detail: First season with VAR. The PL's own figures: correct key decisions rose from 82% (2018-19) to 94%.
quote: In 2018/19, before VAR was introduced, the percentage of correct key match decisions was 82 per cent.
note: Exact date of the first VAR match not captured.

event: FSA survey: VAR made watching football less enjoyable
detail: More than 33,000 fans. 95% of fans who'd seen VAR in stadiums and 94% on TV said less enjoyable; 44% of regular match-goers said they'd attend less.
quote: 95 per cent of fans who had experienced VAR in stadiums and 94 per cent who had watched matches on TV
note: Sample given as 'more than 33,000' (photo caption says 'almost 33,000'). Covers all fans, not only Premier League.

event: Thicker offside lines and a higher bar for VAR intervention
detail: Overlapping thick lines now count as onside (benefit to the attacker), and a higher threshold for 'clear and obvious' errors.
quote: We then put on the thicker broadcast lines and where they overlap, those situations will now be deemed as onside.
note: Quote is Mike Riley's. Effective from the start of 2021-22.

event: Everton 0-1 Man City: Rodri handball not penalised
detail: VAR checked but referee Chris Kavanagh's no-penalty call stood. Earliest public PGMOL admission in FourFourTwo's list.
quote: Everton chairman Bill Kenwright and manager Frank Lampard both received phone calls from then chief Mike Riley
note: Date from 90min; FourFourTwo gives February 2022.

event: Independent KMI panel introduced
detail: Five members: three former players or coaches, one Premier League rep, one refereeing-body rep. Public VAR error counts start from this season.
quote: The KMI Panel was introduced during the 2022/23 season.
note: Exact start date not given; dated to the season start. Page (Aug 2026) names the refereeing body 'Pro Ref'.

event: Crystal Palace 3-1 Aston Villa: penalty given for Digne handball after VAR check
quote: Villa were handed an apology.

event: Howard Webb named PGMOL chief refereeing officer
detail: Replaces Mike Riley, whose departure was announced in June 2022.
quote: Howard Webb is to become the new chief refereeing officer of the Premier League when Mike Riley steps down.
note: Start date not given in the article (widely reported as 1 December 2022; not verified here).

event: Chelsea 2-1 West Ham: West Ham goal disallowed for Bowen 'foul' on Mendy
quote: Bowen's foul on Mendy was later apologised for.
note: Date from 90min.

event: Newcastle 0-0 Crystal Palace: own goal disallowed for Willock foul on Guaita
quote: officiating group PGMOL have had to issue apologies to Premier League sides on 13 separate occasions
note: One of the 13 incidents both lists give; no incident-specific quote. Date from 90min.

event: Man Utd 3-1 Arsenal: Martinelli goal ruled out for Odegaard foul on Eriksen
quote: PGMOL later admitted Arsenal should have been 1-0 up.

event: Fulham 3-0 Aston Villa: Douglas Luiz sent off after VAR intervention
quote: PGMOL apologised for the VAR's incorrect intervention in the incident.
note: Date from 90min.

event: Nottingham Forest 2-2 Brentford: Brentford penalty for Wissa/Henderson contact
quote: officiating group PGMOL have had to issue apologies to Premier League sides on 13 separate occasions
note: One of the 13 incidents both lists give. Date from 90min.

event: Aston Villa 3-1 Man Utd: wall set more than 10 yards back for Digne free-kick goal
quote: That led to an apology to Man Utd
note: Arguably an on-field error rather than a VAR one.

event: Crystal Palace 1-1 Brighton: Estupinan goal ruled offside with lines drawn in the wrong place
quote: While hugely disappointed by the error, the club has accepted PGMOL's apology
note: Quote is Brighton's statement.

event: Arsenal 1-1 Brentford: Toney goal allowed despite offside in the build-up
detail: VAR Lee Mason; wrong player used for the offside check.
quote: officiating group PGMOL have had to issue apologies to Premier League sides on 13 separate occasions
note: One of the 13 incidents both lists give. Date from 90min.

event: Tottenham 2-1 Brighton: Mitoma penalty not given
detail: VAR didn't send Stuart Attwell to the monitor.
quote: Webb later admitted a penalty should have been awarded.
note: Date from 90min.

event: FSA National Supporters Survey: almost two thirds oppose VAR
detail: 9,645 fans surveyed in March-April 2023. 63.3% oppose VAR, 26.8% in favour; almost 92% say decisions take too long.
quote: Almost two thirds (63.3 per cent) of supporters said they oppose the use of VAR
note: Also: 'Almost 92 per cent said decisions were taking too long to make.' Covers all fans.

event: Man Utd 1-0 Wolves: Onana challenge on Kalajdzic not penalised
quote: officiating group PGMOL have had to issue apologies to Premier League sides on 13 separate occasions
note: One of the 13 incidents both lists give; 90min mentions 'an admission from Jon Moss'. Date from 90min.

event: Match Officials Mic'd Up launches
detail: Howard Webb talks through VAR audio from recent incidents in a regular show.
quote: the first instalment of 'Match Officials: Mic'd Up', led by Howard Webb.
note: Some coverage mentions a pilot in May 2023 (not verified).

event: Tottenham 2-1 Liverpool: Diaz goal wrongly disallowed for offside
detail: VAR Darren England didn't intervene after a miscommunication. The last entry in both apology lists.
quote: quickly admitted a 'significant human error' had occurred.

event: Webb: referees to explain VAR decisions to crowds
detail: Planned from 2024-25; still needed Premier League approval.
quote: referees could soon announce to stadium crowds and television audiences why they have changed their decisions.
note: Actual Premier League start date not yet captured.

event: Clubs vote 19-1 to keep VAR after Wolves' motion to scrap it
detail: Clubs agreed six action points instead: keep a high threshold, cut delays (semi-automated offside), referee announcements, better training, more transparency, a fan campaign.
quote: clubs voting 19-1 on Thursday to keep the video assistant.
note: Wolves' reasons (lost celebrations, hostility to officials, time taken over decisions) come from a search summary, not verified here.

event: 'Referee's call' replaces the 'clear and obvious' wording
quote: introduced at the start of the season to effectively replace 'clear and obvious.'
note: Dated to the season start.

event: Semi-automated offside technology first used
detail: Planned for autumn 2024, delayed after testing problems.
quote: The Premier League will introduce semi-automated offside technology for the first time on Saturday April 12.

event: FSA survey: three in four Premier League fans don't support VAR
detail: Nearly 8,000 fans. 75.71% don't support VAR; more than 90% say it removed the joy of goal celebrations; more than 70% disagree it improved accuracy.
quote: Asked if they support the use of VAR in football, meanwhile, 75.71% said they do not
note: Premier League fans only. Also: more than 97% oppose 'VAR makes watching football more enjoyable'.

event: Premier League: its own research says fans want VAR kept but improved
quote: Search snippet only: Premier League research indicates fans are largely in favour of keeping VAR
note: Find the PL's own statement or research before using this.

event: Premier League announces weekly publication of KMI panel verdicts
detail: The per-incident data this project is built on.
quote: the Premier League will publish the results of its Key Match Incident (KMI) Panel weekly, on its website and app.
